steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: An operational amplifier (op-amp) is a high-gain differential amplifier with two inputs: inverting (−) and non-inverting (+). | Key Fact: The ideal op-amp has infinite open-loop gain, infinite input impedance, zero output impedance and infinite bandwidth. | Key Fact: A real op-amp has very high but finite open-loop gain (typically 10⁵ to 10⁶), high input impedance and low output impedance. | Key Fact: Negative feedback is used to control gain and improve stability; it reduces overall gain to a predictable value set by external components.
